search_scope: The three reviewed syntheses listed in docs/phenome-mapping-rules.md (Docs A, B, and C). No primary sources were opened, so every estimate remains `unverified` (R1).
ascertainment_boundary: Coded and diagnosed comorbidity only. The map cannot see undiagnosed disease, conditions never coded, deaths before outcome ascertainment, care delivered outside the data system, or phenotypes that predate the index diagnosis (R35). PheWAS over UKB/MVP/All of Us and the 145,000-patient analysis see coded comorbidity, and the number of conditions a body has is not the number a database contains.

rule_tensions.description: Tier B is graded on a single data system (Swedish national registers). R16 requires the same association from >=2 populations that do not overlap in subjects, institution, or data system.
rule_tensions.resolution: pending reviewer decision: either cite the corroborating population the sources imply, or regrade to C

rule_tensions.description: Tier A requires a CI that excludes 1.00 to be recorded. The source reports a dose-response (1.4 / 1.5 / 1.8) and states the CI excludes 1, but does not print the interval.
rule_tensions.resolution: pending primary-source verification: add the printed CI (R1) or regrade to B

rule_tensions.description: Tier A requires the effect to persist under adjustment. This row attenuates under adjustment for obesity (Doc B: attenuates but does not eliminate; Doc A: often attenuates or eliminates), which is why it also carries the M modifier.
rule_tensions.resolution: pending reviewer decision: accept an M-modifier A row whose attenuation state is 'attenuates', or regrade to B + M

rule_tensions.description: Tier A requires the effect to persist under adjustment. The pooled estimate (1.75) attenuates to 1.77 in the most-adjusted veteran analysis — it remains significant, but the row's attenuation state is 'attenuates' rather than 'persists'.
rule_tensions.resolution: pending review: either record a persists-state estimate from a population where the fully adjusted model is printed, or hold the row at A with this tension declared

rule_tensions.description: Tier B requires the mandatory adjustment set to be at least asserted. The insomnia synthesis reports the association without enumerating adjustment.
rule_tensions.resolution: pending review: promote the row's adjustment set to 'asserted' if the primary source names its covariates, or regrade to C

open_items.item: No row is verified. Every estimate is still as-stated by the three syntheses; R1 promotion requires opening each primary source and confirming estimator, value, CI, population, and follow-up.

Domain coverage in this version: domains 1–5, 7–13, and 15 carry at least one row (domains 4, 8, 10, 11, and 13 as explicit D rows — recorded as findings, never as evidence of no association, R43). Domains 6, 14, 16, 17, 18, 19, and 20 still have no row: a declared coverage gap, not a null finding.

The §15 grade table is only partly materialized. New in 1.1.0: severe infection (tier B, domain 15) and the trauma stratum of the functional-somatic contrast (domain 12, R7). Still declared and absent: ME/CFS, the PTSD stratum of the functional-somatic contrast, the chronic-TMD prevalence row, leukocyte telomere length, endothelial/inflammatory intermediates, the neurodegenerative biomarker row, all-cause mortality year 1 and >1 year, post-MI PTSD, PTSD after trauma by sleep reactivity, and the R45 attribution-exception row (maternal autoimmune → offspring CVD).

Unmaterialized rule tensions, recorded rather than waived: the neurodegenerative biomarker row (tier B on one population, relying on R40 m2 as an R16 exception); all-cause mortality >1 year (tier B on one registry); the PTSD-stratum functional-somatic and chronic-TMD rows; and the iatrogenic domain, whose content is mechanism-only with no epidemiological estimate to verify.

The §12 sweep has no domain for dermatologic, lymphatic, urologic/genital, or congenital/developmental outcomes. The 1.4.0 vocabulary cross-check (src/phenome/sequelae-crosswalk.ts) reports those conditions as domain-gap marks or not-a-sequela exclusions rather than forcing them into an unrelated domain.

Shared-cohort dependency is not disclosed in the sources: the same Swedish registry supplies the autoimmune, infection, and mortality rows, and the same NHS II cohort supplies CVD, T2D, SLE, and telomere findings (R16).
Publication bias and heterogeneity reporting is thin throughout, with one explicit warning that CRP meta-analyses are highly heterogeneous — which caps those estimates well below precise (R15).
The map is unsigned, so it cannot claim completeness under §0 condition 7 even though coverage, tiers, and verification are all recorded. Reviewers are still null.
